already_selected.name: PreFT
already_selected.reason: NeurIPS 2026 (confirmed in the accepted list; the sweep had it as arXiv-only), from the ReFT authors, with a vLLM implementation. It applies a LoRA/ReFT adapter only to prefill tokens and drops it for decode, a token-time locus the atlas's locus axis has no entry for. 1.9x throughput serving 512 adapters.

already_selected.name: OrthoMerge
already_selected.reason: ICML 2026 (verified), Weiyang Liu's group. Merges OFT rotations in the Lie algebra of O(n) and extends to LoRA and full fine-tuning via a Procrustes orthogonal-plus-residual split. It is the first merging rule native to the multiplicative family.

already_selected.name: PRISM
already_selected.reason: ICML 2026 oral/spotlight (verified). Puts DP noise on the gauge-invariant tangent space of Z=BA rather than on the factors, which removes the bilinear noise amplification of naive DP-LoRA. It is the clearest 2026 algorithm built on LoRA's GL(r) fibre.

already_selected.name: KeepLoRA
already_selected.reason: ICLR 2026 (verified) and the most-cited 2026 PEFT method in the sweep (S2 23). Continual LoRA whose gradient is projected onto the residual subspace orthogonal to the pretrained principal subspace and to past-task features. A natural successor to O-LoRA, InfLoRA and SD-LoRA.

already_selected.name: LoRA-Pre
already_selected.reason: ICLR 2026 Oral (verified). Recasts Adam/Muon EMA momenta as online linear regression and keeps optimizer states in low-rank factored form. Matches GaLore-type baselines at 1/8 the rank and beats LoRA at equal rank in fine-tuning.

already_selected.name: StructLoRA
already_selected.reason: ACL 2026, S2 14 (second-most cited in the sweep). An information-bottleneck filter prunes task-irrelevant LoRA directions, and a training-only graph coordinator enforces cross-layer consistency, so inference cost is zero.

already_selected.name: FedRot-LoRA
already_selected.reason: ICML 2026 (verified), S2 9. Aligns client LoRA factors by orthogonal rotation before averaging, i.e. fixes the gauge of BA before aggregation, with a convergence bound on aggregation error.

already_selected.name: RLPO / RLMO
already_selected.reason: ICML 2026 (verified). It was excluded on 2026-10-01 as too new, but the acceptance now meets the bar. Shows orthonormal init minimises the LoRA-vs-full-FT gap under RLVR, gives principal and minor-subspace variants, and explains why PiSSA/MiLoRA destabilise RL.

already_selected.name: NaRA
already_selected.reason: ICML 2026 (verified). dW = B C(t) A, where a shared hypernetwork generates the r x r core from the diffusion noise level. It is the first noise-conditioned LoRA for diffusion LLMs and is mergeable only per noise level, a new value on the mergeability axis.

already_selected.name: LiME
already_selected.reason: ICML 2026 spotlight (verified). MoE-PEFT built from one shared PEFT module modulated by lightweight expert vectors, with zero-parameter routing from frozen and adapted representations. Experts are no longer copies of the adapter.

already_selected.name: AGZO
already_selected.reason: ICML 2026 (verified). Zeroth-order fine-tuning with perturbations restricted to the activation-spanned subspace (a linear layer's gradient lies in the span of its inputs). Provably better aligned with the true gradient than isotropic MeZO.

already_selected.name: ZO-Muon
already_selected.reason: Strongest citation signal among arXiv-only items (S2 11, 3 influential, in 7 months; Hong/Yin). Low-rank subspace ZO combined with Muon orthogonalisation, a 'low-rank Muon' for ZO that needs 24.7% of MeZO's queries.

already_selected.name: FlexLoRA (entropy-guided)
already_selected.reason: ICLR 2026 (verified), released in Chongjie Si's Subspace-Tuning codebase. Rank pruning and expansion under a global budget, scored by spectral-energy entropy, with zero-impact init for added directions. Give it a distinct id: it is not the 2024 federated FlexLoRA (2402.11505).

already_selected.name: FourierMoE
already_selected.reason: NeurIPS 2026 (confirmed in the accepted list; the sweep had it as arXiv-only). A frequency-adaptive router sends tokens to experts that each learn conjugate-symmetric spectral coefficients with lossless IDFT. It combines FourierFT with MoE-LoRA.

already_selected.name: SMoA
already_selected.reason: NeurIPS 2026 (confirmed in the accepted list). Hadamard-modulated low-rank branches on aligned spectral diagonal blocks cover more pretrained singular directions per parameter. A new member of the HiRA/MoSA line.

already_selected.name: Bayesian-LoRA
already_selected.reason: ICML 2026 (verified). Shows LoRA is the zero-uncertainty limit of a Kronecker-factored sparse-GP posterior; up to 84% ECE reduction. Belongs beside Laplace-LoRA, BLoB and MonteCLoRA. Not the 2024 Bayesian-LoRA (rank/bit gates) that the init-rank notes list as excluded.

already_selected.name: FLoRG
already_selected.reason: ICLR 2026 (verified), S2 7. Trains a single low-rank factor and aggregates its Gram matrix, a gauge-invariant quantity, with Procrustes alignment between rounds. Pair it with FedRot-LoRA as the second federated gauge-fixing scheme.

already_selected.name: LoDA
already_selected.reason: ICML 2026 (verified), S2 10. A projection-energy, task-driven decomposition into shared and truly task-specific LoRA subspaces for continual learning; argues against the null-space-only design of InfLoRA-style methods.

already_selected.name: LRAgent
already_selected.reason: ICML 2026 (verified), S2 10. For multi-LoRA agents, splits the KV cache into a shared base cache plus a low-rank adapter cache, using a shared-A multi-LoRA layout and a Flash-LoRA-Attention kernel. Extends the S-LoRA/Punica serving line.

already_selected.name: GeoRA
already_selected.reason: ACL 2026 Main (arXiv comment). RLVR LoRA initialised on the principal directions of the RL update subspace, with residual components frozen as an anchor. Gives the atlas a direct contrast with RLPO's orthonormal init.

already_selected.name: MatryoshkaLoRA
already_selected.reason: IST Austria DASLab (Alistarh), code released, no venue yet. dW = B P A with a fixed crafted diagonal P so that every prefix rank gets gradient signal. LoRA and DyLoRA are special choices of P, which gives a clean structural unification.

already_selected.name: LoCO
already_selected.reason: IJCAI 2026. Orthogonal FT as a composition of exp(low-rank skew-symmetric) rotations with a parallel approximation of the chain. A Lie-algebra member of the OFT/BOFT/LOFT family.

already_selected.name: Compress-then-Merge (CtM)
already_selected.reason: ICML 2026 (verified), code released. Projects T LoRAs into shared rank-r cores before merging, so the result is a rank-r LoRA by construction. Reverses the merge-then-SVD pipeline and builds on Core Space, which the atlas has.

already_selected.name: SRR (Structured Residual Reconstruction)
already_selected.reason: ICML 2026 (verified). Preserves the top-k singular subspace, quantises only the residual and spends the remaining rank on error reconstruction. Gives a Q+LR start for QPEFT in the LoftQ/LQ-LoRA line (+5.9 GLUE at 2-bit).

already_selected.name: Prompt2Effect
already_selected.reason: ECCV 2026 (Snap). A hypernetwork conditioned on the prompt and on the frozen base weights emits LoRAs in one pass, using an SVD-canonicalised parameterisation that removes the factorisation (gauge) ambiguity. Extends the T2L/D2L generation line.

already_selected.name: GiVA
already_selected.reason: AISTATS 2026. Gradient-informed frozen bases for VeRA-style vector adaptation reach LoRA-level accuracy at 8x lower rank with VeRA-level parameter counts. Addresses VeRA's main weakness, the high rank it needs.

already_selected.name: Activation Prompt (AP)
already_selected.reason: AISTATS 2026, S2 14. Generalises input-level visual prompting to universal additive perturbations on intermediate activation maps and analyses why input-only VP lags. Links VP/VPT to activation-editing methods (RED, LoFiT).

already_selected.name: Stable-LoRA
already_selected.reason: ICLR 2026 (verified). Proves LoRA self-stabilises feature learning except that the non-zero A init breaks it, and fixes this by shrinking A in the first steps at no memory cost. Complements the Hayou init-dynamics and LoRA+ entries.

already_selected.name: MDPD
already_selected.reason: CVPR 2026. Memory-efficient side-network tuning in which backbone and side network distil into each other, then the side network is dropped at inference. A training-only side network is new for the adapters family, which otherwise gets no 2026 member.

theory_suggestions_all.title: Learning Rate Scaling across LoRA Ranks and Transfer to Full Finetuning
theory_suggestions_all.claim: Maximal-Update Adaptation (muA), a muP-style theory for LoRA (Chen, Villar, Hayou; ICML 2026; S2 ~10). The optimal learning rate is either rank-invariant or scales inversely with rank, depending on initialisation and the LoRA scaling factor. This lets LR transfer across ranks and to full fine-tuning.

theory_suggestions_all.title: Uniform Spectral Growth and Convergence of Muon in LoRA-Style Matrix Factorization
theory_suggestions_all.claim: Under spectral gradient flow (continuous-time Muon) on LoRA factors, all singular values of BA grow at equal rates. This contrasts with largest-first incremental learning under plain gradient flow. The flow converges to a global minimum from almost every initialisation (Chulhee Yun group; S2 ~8).

theory_suggestions_all.title: When pre-training hurts LoRA fine-tuning: a dynamical analysis via single-index models
theory_suggestions_all.claim: For one-pass-SGD LoRA on single-index models, excessive pre-training can slow fine-tuning. The convergence rate is characterised exactly through initial alignment and the target's nonlinearity (Loureiro, Barbier).

theory_suggestions_all.title: Rank-Accuracy Trade-off for LoRA: A Gradient-Flow Analysis
theory_suggestions_all.claim: LoRA gradient-flow equations are identical for simultaneous and sequential factor updates. The paper gives closed-form rank-vs-accuracy relations for trace-squared and Frobenius low-rank approximation losses.

theory_suggestions_all.title: Why LoRA Resists Label Noise: A Theoretical Framework for Noise-Robust Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
theory_suggestions_all.claim: Rank-r LoRA cannot memorise arbitrary labels once n exceeds O(r(d+k-r)). The optimal rank balances approximation bias against noise variance and decreases as the noise rate rises.

theory_suggestions_all.title: Subspace Geometry Governs Catastrophic Forgetting in Low-Rank Adaptation
theory_suggestions_all.claim: LoRA forgetting follows F = alpha(1 - cos^2 theta_min) + beta, where theta_min is the minimum principal angle between task gradient subspaces. Forgetting is roughly rank-invariant at high angles, and rank only matters when task subspaces are similar.

theory_suggestions_all.title: Weight Updates as Activation Shifts: A Principled Framework for Steering
theory_suggestions_all.claim: Proves a first-order equivalence between activation-space interventions and weight-space updates, with conditions under which steering replicates fine-tuning. It identifies the post-block output as the most expressive intervention site (ICML 2026).

theory_suggestions_all.title: Linearization Explains Fine-Tuning in Large Language Models
theory_suggestions_all.claim: With an explicit Euclidean proximity bias, fine-tuning dynamics are equivalent to learning with a positive-definite NTK. The NTK eigenspectrum correlates with adaptation performance, and the paper gives spectral perturbation bounds for PEFT layer choice.

theory_suggestions_all.title: Understanding and Guiding Layer Placement in Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models
theory_suggestions_all.claim: A projected-residual view of PEFT. Under a local quadratic model, the benefit of adapting a layer is governed by its projected residual norm (a normalised gradient norm), activation energy and inter-layer coupling, which gives a principled layer-selection rule.

theory_suggestions_all.title: LoRA and Privacy: When Random Projections Help (and When They Don't)
theory_suggestions_all.claim: Noise-free LoRA-style random projection is not differentially private, shown by a membership-inference attack with AUC > 0.99. The noisy variant gets privacy amplification from randomness plus low rank, and LoRA is an instance of the matrix-valued mechanism.

theory_suggestions_all.title: The Blessing of Dimensionality in LLM Fine-tuning: A Variance-Curvature Perspective
theory_suggestions_all.claim: Fine-tuning landscapes have low-dimensional curvature: a few high-curvature directions dominate. This explains why evolution strategies or zeroth-order methods work with about 30 samples, and why rewards rise then degrade under ES and GRPO (Fiete, Miikkulainen; S2 ~8).

theory_suggestions_all.title: Why Does Adaptive Zeroth-Order Optimization Work?
theory_suggestions_all.claim: The empirical std of ZO loss differences is proportional to the gradient norm with high probability. Under (L0,L1)-smoothness this gives faster rates and better query complexity for adaptive ZO methods than for fixed-step MeZO-style ones.

theory_suggestions_all.title: Model Evolution Under Zeroth-Order Optimization: A Neural Tangent Kernel Perspective
theory_suggestions_all.claim: Introduces the Neural Zeroth-order Kernel. For linear and linearised models its expectation is constant during ZO training, which gives closed-form function-space dynamics of ZO fine-tuning.

theory_suggestions_all.title: A Unified Generalization Framework for Model Merging: Trade-offs, Non-Linearity, and Scaling Laws
theory_suggestions_all.claim: An L2-stability analysis splits merged-model excess risk into optimisation and generalisation terms. It proves an optimisation-generalisation trade-off that explains merging collapse when experts are over-trained, covering task arithmetic and AdaMerging.

theory_suggestions_all.title: Understanding LoRA as Knowledge Memory: An Empirical Analysis
theory_suggestions_all.claim: Empirical paper, not theory (ICML 2026; S2 ~13). A systematic study of how much knowledge a LoRA can store as modular parametric memory and how such modules compose.

theory_suggestions_all.title: The Appeal and Reality of Recycling LoRAs with Adaptive Merging
theory_suggestions_all.claim: Empirical paper (ICML 2026). With about 1,000 real Hugging Face LoRAs for Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, adaptive LoRA merging and recycling methods give limited gains over simple baselines.

theory_suggestions_all.title: High-Dimensional Theory of LoRA Fine-Tuning in a Solvable Attention Model
theory_suggestions_all.claim: Gives a sharp high-dimensional asymptotic characterisation of pretraining followed by rank-1 LoRA in single-head attention, via order parameters. Predicts test error and representation alignment as functions of pretraining quality.

theory_suggestions_all.title: LoRA vs. Full Fine-Tuning: A Theoretical Perspective
theory_suggestions_all.claim: In linear regression, LoRA has lower excess risk than full fine-tuning when the pretraining-to-downstream shift is effectively low-rank, in both over- and under-determined regimes. Explains why very small ranks can generalise better.

theory_suggestions_all.title: Convergent Stochastic Training of Multi-Headed Attention and Understanding LoRA
theory_suggestions_all.claim: Under mild regularisation, the Gibbs measures of LoRA on a shallow net and of multi-head attention satisfy a Poincaré inequality. For LoRA the constant is independent of data dimension, which gives provable trainability by stochastic methods.

theory_suggestions_all.title: Rethinking the Rank Threshold for LoRA Fine-Tuning
theory_suggestions_all.claim: The LoRA manifold dimension r(m+n)−r² gives a weaker capacity requirement (r(m+n)−r² > C*·KN, C*≈1.35), met at r=1 for binary classification. Under cross-entropy, the PL inequality removes the rank threshold entirely.

theory_suggestions_all.title: Catastrophic Forgetting is Low-Rank: A Function-Space Theory for Continual Adaptation
theory_suggestions_all.claim: In the NTK regime, old-task prediction drift is driven by the cross-task kernel. This gives a closed-form forgetting predictor before any gradient step and shows forgetting is low-rank (frozen-backbone PEFT continual learning). ICML 2026 workshop.

theory_suggestions_all.title: Pretraining Induces a Reusable Spectral Basis for Downstream Task Adaptation
theory_suggestions_all.claim: Downstream fine-tuning operates within stable pretrained singular directions. Freezing the singular vectors and training only the leading spectral coefficients is competitive on GLUE with 0.2% of parameters.

theory_suggestions_all.title: The Hidden Power of Scaling Factor in LoRA Optimization
theory_suggestions_all.claim: LoRA's α and the learning rate are not interchangeable; α is the main driver of effective optimisation. A Signal-Drift framework explains LoRA's spectral suppression and why standard hyperparameters are too conservative.

theory_suggestions_all.title: Direction-Magnitude Decomposition for Low-Rank Matrix Optimization: Faster Convergence and Saddle-to-saddle Dynamics
theory_suggestions_all.claim: Splitting low-rank factors into direction and magnitude (as in DoRA) provably speeds convergence of matrix factorisation even when the true rank is unknown. Characterises over-parameterised and incremental saddle-to-saddle regimes.

theory_suggestions_all.title: How LoRA Remembers? A Parametric Memory Law for LLM Finetuning
theory_suggestions_all.claim: Fits a power law linking loss reduction ΔL to effective LoRA parameters and sequence length, and finds a token-level phase transition: p>0.5 is sufficient for verbatim greedy recall. Motivates the MemFT budget reallocation.

theory_suggestions_all.title: Zeroth-Order Optimization at the Edge of Stability
theory_suggestions_all.claim: Analyses edge-of-stability dynamics for zeroth-order (MeZO-type) optimisers used in memory-efficient fine-tuning. ICML 2026.

theory_suggestions_all.title: Learning Dynamics of Zeroth-Order Optimization: A Kernel Perspective
theory_suggestions_all.claim: Gives a kernel (NTK-style) account of how ZO fine-tuning updates propagate across examples, explaining ZO learning dynamics. ICML 2026.

theory_suggestions_all.title: Why Zeroth-Order Adaptation May Forget Less: A Randomized Shaping Theory
theory_suggestions_all.claim: A randomized-shaping theory for why ZO fine-tuning causes less forgetting than first-order fine-tuning.

theory_suggestions_all.title: Subliminal Learning is a LoRA Artifact
theory_suggestions_all.claim: Teacher-to-student subliminal trait transmission depends on LoRA rank in an inverted-U and disappears under full fine-tuning; it is highly context-dependent. The authors note that later work disputes some claims.

theory_suggestions_all.title: On the Convergence of Stochastic Low-Rank Adaptation
theory_suggestions_all.claim: Improves deterministic LoRA-GD complexity from exp(O(eps^-2)) to O(eps^-4) for an eps-stationary point. Gives the first stochastic-LoRA rates: O(eps^-8) for LoRA-NSGDM and a better rate with variance reduction (LoRA-STORM) under mean-square smoothness. John C.S. Lui group.

theory_suggestions_all.title: The Intruder Threshold: A Spectral Law for LoRA Fine-Tuning
theory_suggestions_all.claim: Derives a per-layer critical update strength s* = θ/(γ σ1(BA)) from the pretrained spectrum alone, using a rectangular spiked-deformation transform. It predicts when intruder dimensions (linked to forgetting) appear, within a factor of two on 82% of 9,840 layer scans, with no fitted parameters.

theory_suggestions_all.title: How Much Rank Does LoRA Need? Rank-Error Bounds for Transformer Attention
theory_suggestions_all.claim: Task-dependent upper and lower bounds on the best KL error of a rank-r query LoRA update to a pretrained attention head. The bounds scale as psi(||d||) with psi(t)=min(t^2,t), where d is the attention-score gap.

theory_suggestions_all.title: What Does the Rank Buy? A Spectral and Distributional Analysis of Low-Rank Adaptation
theory_suggestions_all.claim: Under per-factor norm budgets, the updates LoRA can reach form a nuclear-norm ball intersected with rank<=r, and every complexity or displacement functional is maximized at rank one. So Rademacher complexity and distribution shift are rank-independent: rank does not control capacity.

theory_suggestions_all.title: When Can Prefixes Compile LoRA? Exact Resource-Capped Tests for Frozen Attention
theory_suggestions_all.claim: Gives exact conditions (observability, realizability via a second-order-cone program, implementation with 2r signed slots) under which a fixed continuous prefix can replicate a given low-rank adapter on a frozen attention head. Connects prefix-tuning and LoRA expressivity.

theory_suggestions_all.title: A Dynamical Theory of LoRA in Continual Learning
theory_suggestions_all.claim: Asymptotically exact ODE description of LoRA fine-tuning on a second task in a solvable teacher-student model. Low rank reduces interference with task-1 features, but the standard initialization slows adaptation to the new task.

theory_suggestions_all.title: Certification Frontiers for Gaussian LoRA: Independent Priors, Posterior Risk, and Prediction-Preserving Balancing
theory_suggestions_all.claim: Characterizes when Gaussian LoRA posteriors give non-vacuous PAC-Bayes certificates. Includes an exact isotropic KL envelope and closed-form KL minimization over the GL(r) gauge symmetry of the low-rank factors.

theory_suggestions_all.title: Tight Sample Complexity for Low-Rank Adaptation: Matching Bounds and Rank Selection
theory_suggestions_all.claim: Matching upper and minimax lower bounds, O~(rd/n) and Omega(rd/n), on excess risk for rank-r LoRA, with a rank-selection dichotomy. Single author, Springer submission.

theory_suggestions_all.title: Predicting When Random Low-Dimensional Reparameterizations Train Neural Networks
theory_suggestions_all.claim: Conic and statistical-dimension theory with a quadratic master formula that predicts the latent dimension a frozen random map needs (intrinsic-dimension / VeRA-style PEFT) to reach low loss.

theory_suggestions_all.title: Reducing the Adaptation Gap Through Reachable Fisher Geometry
theory_suggestions_all.claim: Defines the reachable Fisher (full-model Fisher pulled back through the adapter Jacobian) and shows when adapter choice provably widens subgroup performance gaps. The Fisher trace alone loses this information.

theory_suggestions_all.title: How Many Bits Can an Adapter Write? Measuring the Capacity and Memorization of Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
theory_suggestions_all.claim: Compression-based measurement finds a couple of bits stored per trainable adapter parameter. Capacity depends on where the parameters sit (MLP holds about 2x attention) and on the structure of the frozen base, and privacy leakage grows with the bits written.

theory_suggestions_all.title: Behaviorally Effective LoRA Writes Are Sparse and Structured
theory_suggestions_all.claim: Empirical study: converting a trained LoRA's write columns into a frozen orthonormal basis and continuing training is lossless (<=0.25% Frobenius error). The behaviour-carrying part of the update is far sparser than rank suggests.

theory_suggestions_all.title: Diffract: Spectral View of LLM Domain Adaptation
theory_suggestions_all.claim: ICML 2026 spotlight. Continual pre-training leaves singular values nearly unchanged and adapts mainly singular vectors. Up to 60% of attention-head updates can be rewound without loss.

theory_suggestions_all.title: Routing Is Not Enough: Diagnosing Intra-Adapter Subspace Contention in MoE+LoRA Fine-Tuning
theory_suggestions_all.claim: EMNLP 2026 Findings. Interference in MoE+LoRA comes from nearly orthogonal domain gradients competing inside the same low-rank adapter subspace, not from routing overlap. Proposes SpawnLoRA as a remedy.

theory_suggestions_all.title: Riemannian Structure and Optimization for a Class of Low-Parametric Orthogonal Matrices
theory_suggestions_all.claim: Shows when block-diagonal-times-permutation orthogonal matrices (the BOFT/Monarch family used in orthogonal fine-tuning) form a smooth manifold, and gives efficient Riemannian tools for the two-factor case.

theory_suggestions_all.title: Super Weights in LLMs and the Failure of Selective Training
theory_suggestions_all.claim: COLM 2026. Training only super-weight coordinates (100 to 36K parameters) collapses accuracy, while equally many random coordinates or LoRA work. Evidence against magnitude-salience-based sparse fine-tuning.

theory_suggestions_all.title: Dive Into the Implicit Biases of Low-rank Vision-language Alignment

theory_suggestions_all.title: New Hybrid Fine-Tuning Paradigm for LLMs: Algorithm Design and Convergence Analysis Framework

theory_suggestions_all.title: How does the optimizer implicitly bias the model merging loss landscape?

ICLR 2026 poster; arXiv 2025-10-06; S2 cites 2.

theory_suggestions_all.title: Specialization after Generalization: Towards Understanding Test-Time Training in Foundation Models
theory_suggestions_all.claim: Argues foundation models are globally underparameterised. Under a linear-representation / sparse-concept assumption, test-time training (as used by test-time LoRA methods such as PERK) helps in-distribution by specialising capacity to the local task, with bounds on when it helps. ICLR 2026 poster; arXiv 2025-09-29; S2 cites 6.

theory_suggestions_all.title: On the Convergence Rate of LoRA Gradient Descent
theory_suggestions_all.claim: ICML 2026 oral/spotlight. First non-asymptotic convergence analysis of vanilla LoRA gradient descent with no Lipschitz-smoothness or boundedness assumptions. theory_suggestions_all.title: Learning Rate Scaling across LoRA Ranks and Transfer to Full Finetuning

theory_suggestions_all.title: Towards Understanding the Dynamics of Low-Rank Adaptation
theory_suggestions_all.claim: ICML 2026 (OpenReview https://openreview.net/forum?id=dPvcpbbLSs ; no arXiv found). LoRA updates evolve within the subspace A^T (A A^T)^+ A, and the paper analyses how properties of A at initialisation (e.g. orthogonality versus Gaussian) govern performance.

theory_suggestions_all.title: Understanding Catastrophic Forgetting In LoRA via Mean-Field Attention Dynamics
theory_suggestions_all.claim: ICML 2026 (substantially new v2, May 2026). theory_suggestions_all.title: Spectral Imbalance Causes Forgetting in Low-Rank Continual Adaptation
theory_suggestions_all.claim: ICML 2026. LoRA updates have very imbalanced singular spectra, which drives backward and forward forgetting. EBLoRA decouples magnitude from direction and optimises on a restricted Stiefel manifold; it could also be listed as a method.

theory_suggestions_all.title: Learning Dynamics of Zeroth-Order Optimization: A Kernel Perspective
theory_suggestions_all.claim: ICML 2026. The one-step dynamics of ZO-SGD are governed by an eNTK whose entries are randomly projected tangent-vector inner products (Johnson-Lindenstrauss). theory_suggestions_all.title: Zeroth-Order Optimization at the Edge of Stability
theory_suggestions_all.claim: ICML 2026 (Niao He, Sewoong Oh et al.). Mean-square stability of two-point ZO methods depends on the whole Hessian spectrum, and in practice they sit at an edge of stability that regularises the Hessian trace, whereas first-order methods regularise the top eigenvalue.

theory_suggestions_all.title: When Shared Knowledge Hurts: Spectral Over-Accumulation in Model Merging
theory_suggestions_all.claim: ICML 2026. Additive merging over-counts shared singular directions and inflates singular values. Singular Value Calibration (SVC), training- and data-free, rescales them and improves Task Arithmetic by 13%.

theory_suggestions_all.title: Revisiting the Role of Pretrained Weights in Model Merging: On Near-Optimality within the Core Subspace
theory_suggestions_all.claim: ICML 2026 (OpenReview https://openreview.net/forum?id=NrGCh79ANM ; no arXiv found). Core Subspace Preservation (CSP) therefore projects merged task vectors onto its orthogonal complement.

theory_suggestions_all.title: Model Merging Scaling Laws in Large Language Models

theory_suggestions_all.title: Message Tuning Outshines Graph Prompt Tuning: A Prismatic Space Perspective
theory_suggestions_all.claim: ICML 2026. Prismatic Space Theory upper-bounds the adaptation capacity of graph prompt tuning. Message Tuning (learnable message prototypes in each GNN layer) provably exceeds that bound.

theory_suggestions_all.title: Look Within or Look Beyond? A Theoretical Comparison Between Parameter-Efficient and Full Fine-Tuning
theory_suggestions_all.claim: ACL 2026. The PEFT solution space is a strict subset of full fine-tuning's, with representational-capacity and robustness upper bounds. Each extra sample reduces risk under PEFT by only about k/d of what it does under full fine-tuning.

theory_suggestions_all.title: Why Do More Experts Fail? A Theoretical Analysis of Model Merging

theory_suggestions_all.claim: Matching Õ(rd/n) upper bound and Ω(rd/n) minimax lower bound on rank-r LoRA excess risk, plus a principled rule for choosing the rank.

theory_suggestions_all.title: On the Convergence of Stochastic Low-Rank Adaptation
theory_suggestions_all.claim: Improves the oracle complexity of deterministic LoRA-GD from exp(O(ε⁻²)) to O(ε⁻⁴) and gives convergence rates for stochastic LoRA.

theory_suggestions_all.claim: GaLore's top-r gradient subspace is mostly estimator noise: two same-step estimates from disjoint minibatches differ as much as estimates T steps apart. Holds across 70M–6.9B models.

theory_suggestions_all.title: Beware of the Batch Size: Hyperparameter Bias in Evaluating LoRA
theory_suggestions_all.claim: Contradictory gains reported across LoRA variants largely trace to untuned batch size; tuned vanilla LoRA often matches complex variants (in the same vein as the covered 'Learning Rate Matters').

theory_suggestions_all.title: Do We Need Adam? Surprisingly Strong and Sparse Reinforcement Learning with SGD in LLMs
theory_suggestions_all.claim: Plain SGD in RL post-training of LLMs is competitive and its updates are highly sparse, supporting the small-subnetwork picture of RL fine-tuning (ICML 2026 spotlight).

theory_suggestions_all.title: Subliminal Learning is a LoRA Artifact
theory_suggestions_all.claim: Subliminal trait transmission has an inverted-U dependence on LoRA rank and disappears under full fine-tuning, so it is attributed to the low-rank parametrisation.
